'''Rollie Tesh''' co-designed Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG) with [[Tom Braunlich]]. Braunlich credits him with the ideas that made the game's math work, including [[Destiny]] numbers.<ref name="bp-destiny">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=600s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 10:00–11:03. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref><ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192945/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive].</ref>

== Before Decipher ==

Tesh met Braunlich through chess at Booker T. Washington High School in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and Braunlich got him into ''Pente''. Tesh held an expert chess rating. ''Pente'' inventor Gary Gabrel recruited both as playtesters at Oklahoma State University.<ref name="rfd14-bio">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=62s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 1:02–3:08. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Both became ''Pente'' world champions, and Tesh proposed the Keryo-Pente variant.<ref name="wp-pente">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pente Pente], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008223533/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pente Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="wp-decipher" /> They met [[Warren Holland]] through Pente Games, pitched him a licensed card game while living near Seattle, and designed the [[Star Trek CCG|''Star Trek'' CCG]] (1994).<ref name="rfd14-trek">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=248s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 4:08–6:44. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="st-timeline" /> Living on Bainbridge Island near Wizards of the Coast, they met ''Magic: The Gathering'' designer [[Richard Garfield]].<ref name="bp27">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU&t=546s The Booster Pack #27 — The making of the Star Trek CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (10 August 2022), 9:06–10:30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131804/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU Internet Archive].</ref>

== Designing SWCCG ==

Tesh and Braunlich moved to Virginia Beach in 1995 to work beside Decipher.<ref name="pilot" /> At first only they and Holland worked on the game with a few staff, until [[Jerry Darcy]] and [[Bill Martinson]] joined. Tesh described the pair's role as coming up with the concepts, which Darcy and Martinson then worked out in detail.<ref name="rfd14-sw" />

The core system grew from a base each player builds up. The base became the deck, and the deck became the Force a player spends and loses.<ref name="rfd14-force">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=616s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 10:16–12:19. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Destiny numbers took the place of dice, so the game needed only cards. Strong cards got low destiny.<ref name="rfd14-destiny">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=767s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 12:47–13:19. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="bp-destiny" /> Former Decipher staffer [[Mark Tuttle]] called SWCCG "Tom and Rollie's … game."<ref name="fantha">[https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Guest Interview: Mark Tuttle], Fantha Tracks (15 March 2018). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195155/https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Internet Archive].</ref>

== Later Decipher work ==

Tesh and Braunlich designed the concept of [[Young Jedi]] (1999) from the ''Episode I'' script. Before the film opened, they built a reconstruction of it from details found online and screened it for the team.<ref name="rfd16" /> They also began a ''Harry Potter'' card game for Decipher, which ended when Decipher did not get the license.<ref name="bp-potter">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=3061s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 51:01–53:07. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Tesh is thanked in the credits of the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] rulebook (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive].</ref>

The GeoCities anagram table unscrambles [[Elis Helrot]] as Rollie Tesh.<ref name="ana">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians]</ref>
